item.title: LibreOffice actually works 365 days a year
item.description:
Source: twitter.com

Top Comment:

Well, OpenOffice wouldn't print on Tuesdays:

“ What a fascinating bug!! My wife has complained that open office will never print on Tuesdays!?! Then she demonstrated it. Sure enough, won't print on Tuesday. Other applications print. I think this is the same bug. Here is my guess:

Print to a postscript file. Observe the line: %%CreationDate: (Tue Mar 3 19:47:42 2009)

Change "Tue" to anything else: %%CreationDate: (XTue Mar 3 19:47:42 2009)

Save the file and it prints. Tools like evince work because they simply omit the "CreationDate" tag to begin with.

Now something odd happens when my cups script (I am using the Brother MFC420CN) copies the file to a temp file. Some of the code is rearranged, not sure how or why, but it uses a command called "file" to identify the file as "PostScript". This check would work on the original file you printed, but by the time it runs the check on the temp file, it misidentifies. Normally it would return:

   PostScript document text conforming at level 3.0
But there is another check that happens before the PostScript check. If it finds "Tue" at the fourth byte of the file, it identifies it as:

   Jan 22 14:32:44 MET 1991\011Erlang JAM file - version 4.2
So it's not a problem w/ openoffice.org, cups, or the brother printer drivers. It is a bug in the `file` utility, and documented at https://bugs.launchpad.net/ubuntu/+source/file/+bug/248619. ”

https://bugs.launchpad.net/ubuntu/+source/cupsys/+bug/255161...

item.title: Why Zig over C for Systems Programming
item.description:
Source: www.mtsoukalos.eu

Top Comment:

Zig is a nice language, but those articles always compare new languages against old-style C without use of modern tools. Most of the listed advantages you can have in C as well if you are willing to adopt modern tooling and style: signed overflow checking: sanitizers, errors you can not ignore: [[nodiscard]], slice type which know their size: variably-modified types or span types.

Defer will also appear in C compilers soon, but personally I still think goto-error handling is clearer.

(Rust has an advantage for temporal memory safety, but this does apply to Zig.)

item.title: Relax: JIT compiler for Rust to reduce build times
item.description:
Source: makepad.github.io

Top Comment:

I did a quick test on various of my rust projects. Most of them it failed to run, on one it miscompiles(?) causing a test case to fail. The only project I got it to run without issue is a basic actix-web website. It takes a whole 14 seconds to actually start the web server. A clean compile is only 24s for all dependencies, and a regular incremental debug build is 2.3s.

The hot patching is unusable. It takes 11s to compile the patch after a simple change: (Some("hi") -> None), and then relax gets a compiler error when refreshing the page.

The project where it miscompiles only has a few very basic dependencies; a clean compile takes 1.3s, incremental just 0.25s and tests take ~0.1s. Relax takes a whole 1.4s to run the tests (unsuccessfully).
